task: Web App to Mobile Build Blueprint and Backlog

overall_task_success.commentary: This run gets the central test this task is built around right and is genuinely forthcoming about its own limitations, naming both the reason it paused and a real access gap that could keep the actual reviewers out of the document it just told them was ready. Those are genuine strengths. What keeps this at 4 is that getting there took a real interruption and multiple rounds of layout rework rather than one clean pass, and the access gap itself, even though disclosed, is a real problem sitting underneath an announcement telling reviewers the document is ready for them. I get a correct, honestly caveated backlog that still needs a permissions fix before anyone else can actually see it.

task_accuracy.commentary: The rule to match an existing issue before creating a new one is applied correctly here, the foundation and authentication issue gets matched by its exact summary and updated in place instead of duplicated, the check this task is built to test. The ticket content is grounded, naming technical elements like signing fallbacks, server side protection for admin routes, and the PostgreSQL and Prisma bootstrap rather than vague scope language. The one place I'd still flag is the foundation ticket's own acceptance list, the credential and secret closure bullet is written out in full, then repeated right after with only the word evidence added, a genuine duplicate inside the one section meant to read as a clean checklist.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: one full stop for explicit confirmation before the upload step, a browser session reconnect, and two rounds of attachment layout rework.
efficiency.commentary: This wasn't a single continuous pass. The run stopped partway through and needed permission to continue before the upload and notification work went ahead, then the browser session had to be reconnected before the uploads could proceed. The attachment layout needed two rounds of correction, a nearly empty trailing page across several tab extracts, then one more line that needed a spacing fix after the bigger layout change. Both fixes read as real diligence to me, catching and correcting rendering defects before anything shipped, rather than blind resubmission. Between the stop and the rework, it adds up to real drag against a task meant to move in one pass, even with all of it recovered cleanly.

writing_quality.commentary: The ticket structure is clear and consistent, a phase, dependencies and evidence, a scoped list, and a done section that reads as genuinely checkable. Attaching each relevant tab as its own file rather than a merged bundle means I open exactly the section that matters. The Teams message is notably careful, it states plainly that this is a draft and nothing has shipped. Two things hold this back for me. One payments ticket bullet crams contracts, authorization, pagination, currency, and reconciliation into a single comma packed sentence instead of its own lines. And the blueprint's prose repeatedly ends a paragraph with a trailing file and line source list, useful for tracing a claim but breaking the narrative rhythm each time.

instruction_following.commentary: The match against an existing issue by its exact summary, the cap of four issues, keeping status in To Do only, and the individually attached tab files are all followed correctly, exactly as the brief lays them out, and the Teams message explicitly reinforces that this is a draft only, the framing the brief asks for. The one place this doesn't fully land for me is one the run names itself, the document's sharing state left it visible only to the account that created it, which sits in tension with posting a message telling reviewers it's ready for them to look at.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: one real stop, the run paused entirely before the step to upload files and needed explicit permission before continuing
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: I'd want the document's sharing opened up to the actual reviewers before treating the Teams post as a genuine signal that this is ready for review
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: What this run does best is flag its own real limitations rather than paper over them. It named the exact reason it stopped before the upload step, and separately surfaced, unprompted, that the document might not be reachable by the people the Teams post addressed. That is real, substantive honesty about a limitation that could have shipped silently. Two things cost it here. It needed a real interruption to finish, a full stop requiring my input rather than a brief pause. And once the attachments were up, it never reopens the tickets to see them rendered, the final check stays at the metadata level, filenames and sizes matching what was queued, without a look at the finished page.

citation_quality.commentary: When I check this against the source, the blueprint cites an exact file and line for nearly every claim throughout, architecture, screen inventory, contracts, data model, delivery plan, and risks, well beyond the Secrets tab. The Mobile Stack table goes further, naming the specific vendor source in the same row as each price rather than in one list at the end. The one place this doesn't carry through is the tickets themselves, the descriptions reference the blueprint by link but don't repeat the file and line behind their own scope bullets, so I have to open the doc to trace any one claim back to code.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: When I trace it, there's real, demonstrated visual work here, several rounds of inspecting rendered pages that caught and fixed genuine layout defects before the attachments shipped. But the path on screen also hit real friction beyond the content itself, the browser session needed to be reconnected after the confirmation pause before the uploads could proceed, an extra recovery step that a fully continuous run wouldn't have needed at all. To me, a genuinely careful visual QA process paired with a hiccup at the session level reads as a mixed enough record to sit in the middle of the range rather than higher.
